q: Which term means “Study of interactions among organisms and their environment”?
e: Ecology: Study of interactions among organisms and their environment. Foundation of ecosystem analysis

q: Which term means “Community of organisms interacting with the physical environment”?
e: Ecosystem: Community of organisms interacting with the physical environment. Includes biotic and abiotic components

q: Which term means “Large ecological region defined by climate and dominant vegetation”?
e: Biome: Large ecological region defined by climate and dominant vegetation. Examples include tundra and tropical rainforest

q: Which term means “Natural place where an organism lives”?
e: Habitat: Natural place where an organism lives. Provides resources and conditions for survival

q: Which term means “Functional role and environmental requirements of a species”?
e: Ecological niche: Functional role and environmental requirements of a species. Includes resource use and interactions

q: Which term means “Individuals of the same species in a defined area”?
e: Population: Individuals of the same species in a defined area. Population size changes through births, deaths and migration

q: Which term means “Populations of different species living together”?
e: Community: Populations of different species living together. Species interact through competition, predation and mutualism

q: Which term means “Variety of life at genetic, species and ecosystem levels”?
e: Biodiversity: Variety of life at genetic, species and ecosystem levels. Supports resilience and ecosystem services

q: Which term means “Variation of genes within a species”?
o: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
e: Genetic diversity: Variation of genes within a species. Helps populations adapt to change

q: Which term means “Variety and relative abundance of species”?
e: Species diversity: Variety and relative abundance of species. Includes richness and evenness

q: Which term means “Variety of ecosystems in a region”?
e: Ecosystem diversity: Variety of ecosystems in a region. Includes forests, wetlands and grasslands

q: Which term means “Species naturally restricted to a particular area”?
e: Endemic species: Species naturally restricted to a particular area. Often vulnerable to habitat loss

q: Which term means “Species occurring naturally in an area”?
e: Native species: Species occurring naturally in an area. Not introduced by human activity

q: Which term means “Non-native species causing ecological or economic harm”?
e: Invasive alien species: Non-native species causing ecological or economic harm. Can displace native species

q: Which term means “Species with a disproportionately large ecological effect”?
e: Keystone species: Species with a disproportionately large ecological effect. Removal can restructure an ecosystem

q: Which term means “Species used to assess environmental conditions”?
e: Indicator species: Species used to assess environmental conditions. Lichens may indicate air quality

q: Which term means “Species whose conservation protects many co-occurring species”?
e: Umbrella species: Species whose conservation protects many co-occurring species. Requires large or diverse habitat

q: Which term means “Charismatic species used to mobilize conservation support”?
e: Flagship species: Charismatic species used to mobilize conservation support. Often used in public campaigns

q: Which term means “Linear transfer of energy through feeding relationships”?
e: Food chain: Linear transfer of energy through feeding relationships. Begins with producers in most ecosystems

q: Which term means “Network of interconnected food chains”?
e: Food web: Network of interconnected food chains. Shows multiple feeding pathways

q: Which term means “Feeding position in a food chain or web”?
e: Trophic level: Feeding position in a food chain or web. Energy generally declines at higher levels

q: Which term means “Organism that produces organic matter from inorganic sources”?
e: Primary producer: Organism that produces organic matter from inorganic sources. Plants use photosynthesis

q: Which term means “Organism that feeds on producers”?
e: Primary consumer: Organism that feeds on producers. Commonly an herbivore

q: Which term means “Organism breaking down dead organic material”?
e: Decomposer: Organism breaking down dead organic material. Returns nutrients to ecosystems

q: Which term means “Animal that consumes dead organic matter”?
e: Detritivore: Animal that consumes dead organic matter. Examples include many earthworms

q: Which term means “Conversion of light energy into chemical energy by producers”?
e: Photosynthesis: Conversion of light energy into chemical energy by producers. Consumes carbon dioxide and releases oxygen

q: Which term means “Release of energy from organic molecules”?
e: Cellular respiration: Release of energy from organic molecules. Produces carbon dioxide and water in aerobic respiration

q: Which term means “Movement of carbon among atmosphere, oceans, organisms and rocks”?
e: Carbon cycle: Movement of carbon among atmosphere, oceans, organisms and rocks. Affected by fossil-fuel combustion

q: Which term means “Movement and transformation of nitrogen in ecosystems”?
e: Nitrogen cycle: Movement and transformation of nitrogen in ecosystems. Includes fixation and denitrification

q: Which term means “Movement of water through evaporation, condensation and precipitation”?
e: Water cycle: Movement of water through evaporation, condensation and precipitation. Also called hydrological cycle

q: Which term means “Movement of phosphorus through rocks, soil, water and organisms”?
e: Phosphorus cycle: Movement of phosphorus through rocks, soil, water and organisms. Has no major gaseous phase

q: Which term means “Conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into biologically usable forms”?
e: Nitrogen fixation: Conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into biologically usable forms. Performed by certain microbes and lightning

q: Which term means “Nutrient enrichment causing excessive plant or algal growth”?
e: Eutrophication: Nutrient enrichment causing excessive plant or algal growth. Can lead to oxygen depletion

q: Which term means “Increasing concentration of persistent substances at higher trophic levels”?
e: Biomagnification: Increasing concentration of persistent substances at higher trophic levels. Classic example involves mercury

q: Which term means “Build-up of a substance within an organism over time”?
e: Bioaccumulation: Build-up of a substance within an organism over time. Occurs when uptake exceeds elimination

q: Which term means “Directional change in community composition over time”?
e: Ecological succession: Directional change in community composition over time. Can be primary or secondary

q: Which term means “Succession beginning without developed soil”?
e: Primary succession: Succession beginning without developed soil. May follow lava flows or glacial retreat

q: Which term means “Succession where soil remains after disturbance”?
e: Secondary succession: Succession where soil remains after disturbance. May follow fire or abandoned farming

q: Which term means “Maximum population an environment can sustain over time”?
e: Carrying capacity: Maximum population an environment can sustain over time. Depends on resources and environmental conditions

q: Which term means “Resource or condition restricting population growth”?
e: Limiting factor: Resource or condition restricting population growth. May be food, water, space or temperature

q: Which term means “Population growth at a constant proportional rate”?
e: Exponential growth: Population growth at a constant proportional rate. Produces a J-shaped curve under ideal conditions

q: Which term means “Population growth slowing near carrying capacity”?
e: Logistic growth: Population growth slowing near carrying capacity. Produces an S-shaped curve

q: Which term means “Interaction in which one organism kills and consumes another”?
e: Predation: Interaction in which one organism kills and consumes another. Influences population dynamics

q: Which term means “Interaction in which organisms seek the same limited resource”?
e: Competition: Interaction in which organisms seek the same limited resource. Can occur within or between species

q: Which term means “Interaction benefiting both participating species”?
e: Mutualism: Interaction benefiting both participating species. Pollination is a common example

q: Which term means “Interaction benefiting one species without significant effect on the other”?
e: Commensalism: Interaction benefiting one species without significant effect on the other. One species gains shelter or transport

q: Which term means “Interaction benefiting a parasite while harming its host”?
e: Parasitism: Interaction benefiting a parasite while harming its host. Usually does not immediately kill the host

q: Which term means “Long-term statistical pattern of weather”?
e: Climate: Long-term statistical pattern of weather. Usually assessed over decades

q: Which term means “Short-term atmospheric conditions”?
e: Weather: Short-term atmospheric conditions. Includes temperature, precipitation and wind

q: Which term means “Warming caused by atmospheric absorption and re-emission of infrared radiation”?
e: Greenhouse effect: Warming caused by atmospheric absorption and re-emission of infrared radiation. Natural process intensified by added greenhouse gases

q: Which term means “Gas that absorbs and emits infrared radiation”?
e: Greenhouse gas: Gas that absorbs and emits infrared radiation. Examples include carbon dioxide and methane

q: Which term means “Long-lived greenhouse gas from natural and human sources”?
o: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
e: Carbon dioxide: Long-lived greenhouse gas from natural and human sources. Fossil-fuel burning raises atmospheric concentration

q: Which term means “Potent greenhouse gas with shorter atmospheric lifetime than carbon dioxide”?
e: Methane: Potent greenhouse gas with shorter atmospheric lifetime than carbon dioxide. Emitted by wetlands, fossil fuels and livestock

q: Which term means “Long-lived greenhouse gas and ozone-depleting substance”?
e: Nitrous oxide: Long-lived greenhouse gas and ozone-depleting substance. Major human source is agricultural soil management

q: Which term means “Long-term rise in global average surface temperature”?
e: Global warming: Long-term rise in global average surface temperature. A major component of current climate change

q: Which term means “Long-term change in climate state or variability”?
e: Climate change: Long-term change in climate state or variability. Human influence is the dominant cause of recent warming

q: Which term means “Human intervention to reduce emissions or enhance sinks”?
e: Mitigation: Human intervention to reduce emissions or enhance sinks. Renewable energy and efficiency are examples

q: Which term means “Adjustment to actual or expected climate effects”?
e: Adaptation: Adjustment to actual or expected climate effects. Can reduce harm or exploit beneficial opportunities

q: Which term means “Capacity to absorb disturbance and retain essential functions”?
e: Resilience: Capacity to absorb disturbance and retain essential functions. Applies to communities and ecosystems

q: Which term means “Propensity to be adversely affected”?
e: Vulnerability: Propensity to be adversely affected. Depends on exposure, sensitivity and adaptive capacity

q: Which term means “Potential occurrence of an event causing harm”?
e: Hazard: Potential occurrence of an event causing harm. Examples include floods and heatwaves

q: Which term means “Presence of people, ecosystems or assets in places that could be affected”?
e: Exposure: Presence of people, ecosystems or assets in places that could be affected. A component of climate risk

q: Which term means “Stratospheric region with elevated ozone concentration”?
e: Ozone layer: Stratospheric region with elevated ozone concentration. Absorbs much harmful ultraviolet radiation

q: Which term means “Reduction in stratospheric ozone”?
e: Ozone depletion: Reduction in stratospheric ozone. Strongly linked to chlorofluorocarbons

q: Which term means “Treaty controlling ozone-depleting substances”?
e: Montreal Protocol: Treaty controlling ozone-depleting substances. Adopted in 1987

q: Which term means “Climate treaty aiming to strengthen global response to climate change”?
e: Paris Agreement: Climate treaty aiming to strengthen global response to climate change. Adopted in 2015

q: Which term means “Framework treaty for international climate cooperation”?
o: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
e: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change: Framework treaty for international climate cooperation. Opened for signature in 1992

q: Which term means “Treaty setting emission targets for many developed countries”?
e: Kyoto Protocol: Treaty setting emission targets for many developed countries. Adopted in 1997

q: Which term means “Treaty on conservation, sustainable use and benefit-sharing”?
e: Convention on Biological Diversity: Treaty on conservation, sustainable use and benefit-sharing. Opened for signature in 1992

q: Which term means “Convention regulating international trade in endangered species”?
e: CITES: Convention regulating international trade in endangered species. Uses appendices with different protection levels

q: Which term means “Treaty for conservation and wise use of wetlands”?
e: Ramsar Convention: Treaty for conservation and wise use of wetlands. Adopted in 1971

q: Which term means “Treaty controlling transboundary movements of hazardous wastes”?
e: Basel Convention: Treaty controlling transboundary movements of hazardous wastes. Adopted in 1989

q: Which term means “Treaty controlling persistent organic pollutants”?
e: Stockholm Convention: Treaty controlling persistent organic pollutants. Adopted in 2001

q: Which term means “Treaty protecting health and environment from mercury”?
e: Minamata Convention: Treaty protecting health and environment from mercury. Adopted in 2013

q: Which term means “Land degradation in drylands”?
e: Desertification: Land degradation in drylands. Driven by climatic variation and human activities

q: Which term means “Conversion or removal of forest cover”?
e: Deforestation: Conversion or removal of forest cover. Reduces habitat and carbon storage

q: Which term means “Establishment of forest on land not recently forested”?
e: Afforestation: Establishment of forest on land not recently forested. Can increase carbon stocks when appropriately planned

q: Which term means “Re-establishment of forest on recently forested land”?
e: Reforestation: Re-establishment of forest on recently forested land. Supports restoration and carbon sequestration

q: Which term means “Removal of topsoil by water, wind or other agents”?
o: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
e: Soil erosion: Removal of topsoil by water, wind or other agents. Can reduce agricultural productivity

q: Which term means “Accumulation of salts in soil”?
e: Salinization: Accumulation of salts in soil. Often associated with irrigation and poor drainage

q: Which term means “Land saturated or flooded long enough to support adapted ecosystems”?
e: Wetland: Land saturated or flooded long enough to support adapted ecosystems. Provides flood regulation and habitat

q: Which term means “Salt-tolerant coastal forest ecosystem”?
e: Mangrove: Salt-tolerant coastal forest ecosystem. Protects shorelines and stores carbon

q: Which term means “Marine ecosystem built largely by reef-forming corals”?
e: Coral reef: Marine ecosystem built largely by reef-forming corals. Highly diverse and sensitive to warming

q: Which term means “Loss of symbiotic algae or pigments from stressed corals”?
e: Coral bleaching: Loss of symbiotic algae or pigments from stressed corals. Often triggered by heat stress

q: Which term means “Decline in ocean pH caused mainly by absorbed carbon dioxide”?

q: Which term means “Defined marine area managed for conservation”?
e: Marine protected area: Defined marine area managed for conservation. Protection levels vary

q: Which term means “Geographically defined area managed for long-term conservation”?

q: Which term means “No reasonable doubt that the last individual has died”?
e: Extinct: No reasonable doubt that the last individual has died. Highest final loss category

e: Critically Endangered: Extremely high risk of extinction in the wild. Most severe of the three IUCN threatened categories

q: Which term means “Very high risk of extinction in the wild”?
e: Endangered: Very high risk of extinction in the wild. Threatened category below Critically Endangered and above Vulnerable

q: Which term means “High risk of extinction in the wild”?
e: Vulnerable: High risk of extinction in the wild. Least severe of the three IUCN threatened categories

q: Which term means “Development meeting present needs without compromising future generations”?

q: Which term means “System aiming to reduce waste and keep materials in use”?

q: Which term means “Benefits people obtain from ecosystems”?
e: Ecosystem services: Benefits people obtain from ecosystems. Include provisioning, regulating and cultural services

q: Which term means “Total greenhouse-gas emissions associated with an activity or entity”?
e: Carbon footprint: Total greenhouse-gas emissions associated with an activity or entity. Often expressed as carbon-dioxide equivalent

q: Which term means “Measure of biologically productive area needed to support consumption and absorb wastes”?

q: Which term means “Assessment of environmental impacts across a product's life cycle”?

q: Which term means “Process evaluating likely environmental effects before approval”?
e: Environmental impact assessment: Process evaluating likely environmental effects before approval. Supports informed decision-making

q: Which term means “Introduction of harmful substances or energy into the environment”?
e: Pollution: Introduction of harmful substances or energy into the environment. Can affect air, water or land

q: Which term means “Contamination of the atmosphere by harmful substances”?

q: Which term means “Mixture of airborne solid particles and liquid droplets”?
e: Particulate matter: Mixture of airborne solid particles and liquid droplets. PM2.5 penetrates deeply into lungs

q: Which term means “Acidic deposition formed mainly from sulfur and nitrogen oxides”?
e: Acid rain: Acidic deposition formed mainly from sulfur and nitrogen oxides. Can acidify soils and waters

q: Which term means “Air pollution mixture reducing visibility and harming health”?
e: Smog: Air pollution mixture reducing visibility and harming health. Photochemical smog involves ground-level ozone

q: Which term means “Contamination degrading water quality”?
e: Water pollution: Contamination degrading water quality. Sources include sewage, industry and agriculture

q: Which term means “Harmful change in water temperature from human activity”?
e: Thermal pollution: Harmful change in water temperature from human activity. Can lower dissolved oxygen

q: Which term means “Harmful or excessive environmental sound”?
e: Noise pollution: Harmful or excessive environmental sound. Can affect health and wildlife

q: Which term means “Discarded solid materials from households, industry and other sources”?
e: Solid waste: Discarded solid materials from households, industry and other sources. Managed through prevention, reuse, recycling and disposal

q: Which term means “Waste posing substantial risk because of toxic, reactive or other properties”?
e: Hazardous waste: Waste posing substantial risk because of toxic, reactive or other properties. Requires special handling

q: Which term means “Waste decomposable by microorganisms”?

q: Which term means “Processing waste into materials or products”?
e: Recycling: Processing waste into materials or products. Reduces demand for virgin resources

q: Which term means “Controlled biological decomposition of organic waste”?

q: Which term means “Engineered site for disposal of solid waste”?

q: Ecosystem diversity is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Ecosystem diversity: Variety of ecosystems in a region. Includes forests, wetlands and grasslands

q: Endemic species is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Endemic species: Species naturally restricted to a particular area. Often vulnerable to habitat loss

q: Native species is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Native species: Species occurring naturally in an area. Not introduced by human activity

q: Invasive alien species is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Invasive alien species: Non-native species causing ecological or economic harm. Can displace native species

q: Keystone species is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Keystone species: Species with a disproportionately large ecological effect. Removal can restructure an ecosystem

q: Indicator species is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Indicator species: Species used to assess environmental conditions. Lichens may indicate air quality

q: Umbrella species is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Umbrella species: Species whose conservation protects many co-occurring species. Requires large or diverse habitat

q: Flagship species is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Flagship species: Charismatic species used to mobilize conservation support. Often used in public campaigns

q: Food chain is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Food chain: Linear transfer of energy through feeding relationships. Begins with producers in most ecosystems

q: Food web is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Food web: Network of interconnected food chains. Shows multiple feeding pathways

q: Trophic level is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Trophic level: Feeding position in a food chain or web. Energy generally declines at higher levels

q: Primary producer is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Primary producer: Organism that produces organic matter from inorganic sources. Plants use photosynthesis

q: Primary consumer is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Primary consumer: Organism that feeds on producers. Commonly an herbivore

q: Decomposer is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Decomposer: Organism breaking down dead organic material. Returns nutrients to ecosystems

q: Detritivore is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Detritivore: Animal that consumes dead organic matter. Examples include many earthworms

q: Photosynthesis is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Photosynthesis: Conversion of light energy into chemical energy by producers. Consumes carbon dioxide and releases oxygen

q: Cellular respiration is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Cellular respiration: Release of energy from organic molecules. Produces carbon dioxide and water in aerobic respiration

q: Carbon cycle is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Carbon cycle: Movement of carbon among atmosphere, oceans, organisms and rocks. Affected by fossil-fuel combustion

q: Nitrogen cycle is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Nitrogen cycle: Movement and transformation of nitrogen in ecosystems. Includes fixation and denitrification

q: Water cycle is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Water cycle: Movement of water through evaporation, condensation and precipitation. Also called hydrological cycle

q: Phosphorus cycle is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Phosphorus cycle: Movement of phosphorus through rocks, soil, water and organisms. Has no major gaseous phase

q: Nitrogen fixation is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Nitrogen fixation: Conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into biologically usable forms. Performed by certain microbes and lightning

q: Eutrophication is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Eutrophication: Nutrient enrichment causing excessive plant or algal growth. Can lead to oxygen depletion

q: Biomagnification is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Biomagnification: Increasing concentration of persistent substances at higher trophic levels. Classic example involves mercury

q: Bioaccumulation is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Bioaccumulation: Build-up of a substance within an organism over time. Occurs when uptake exceeds elimination

q: Ecological succession is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Ecological succession: Directional change in community composition over time. Can be primary or secondary

q: Primary succession is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Primary succession: Succession beginning without developed soil. May follow lava flows or glacial retreat

q: Secondary succession is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Secondary succession: Succession where soil remains after disturbance. May follow fire or abandoned farming

q: Carrying capacity is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Carrying capacity: Maximum population an environment can sustain over time. Depends on resources and environmental conditions

q: Limiting factor is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Limiting factor: Resource or condition restricting population growth. May be food, water, space or temperature

q: Exponential growth is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Exponential growth: Population growth at a constant proportional rate. Produces a J-shaped curve under ideal conditions

q: Logistic growth is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Logistic growth: Population growth slowing near carrying capacity. Produces an S-shaped curve

q: Predation is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Predation: Interaction in which one organism kills and consumes another. Influences population dynamics

q: Competition is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Competition: Interaction in which organisms seek the same limited resource. Can occur within or between species

q: Mutualism is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Mutualism: Interaction benefiting both participating species. Pollination is a common example

q: Commensalism is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Commensalism: Interaction benefiting one species without significant effect on the other. One species gains shelter or transport

q: Parasitism is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Parasitism: Interaction benefiting a parasite while harming its host. Usually does not immediately kill the host

q: Climate is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Climate: Long-term statistical pattern of weather. Usually assessed over decades

q: Weather is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Weather: Short-term atmospheric conditions. Includes temperature, precipitation and wind

q: Greenhouse effect is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Greenhouse effect: Warming caused by atmospheric absorption and re-emission of infrared radiation. Natural process intensified by added greenhouse gases

q: Greenhouse gas is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Greenhouse gas: Gas that absorbs and emits infrared radiation. Examples include carbon dioxide and methane

q: Carbon dioxide is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Carbon dioxide: Long-lived greenhouse gas from natural and human sources. Fossil-fuel burning raises atmospheric concentration

q: Methane is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Methane: Potent greenhouse gas with shorter atmospheric lifetime than carbon dioxide. Emitted by wetlands, fossil fuels and livestock

q: Nitrous oxide is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Nitrous oxide: Long-lived greenhouse gas and ozone-depleting substance. Major human source is agricultural soil management

q: Global warming is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Global warming: Long-term rise in global average surface temperature. A major component of current climate change

q: Climate change is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Climate change: Long-term change in climate state or variability. Human influence is the dominant cause of recent warming

q: Mitigation is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Mitigation: Human intervention to reduce emissions or enhance sinks. Renewable energy and efficiency are examples

q: Adaptation is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Adaptation: Adjustment to actual or expected climate effects. Can reduce harm or exploit beneficial opportunities

q: Resilience is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Resilience: Capacity to absorb disturbance and retain essential functions. Applies to communities and ecosystems

q: Vulnerability is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Vulnerability: Propensity to be adversely affected. Depends on exposure, sensitivity and adaptive capacity

q: Hazard is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Hazard: Potential occurrence of an event causing harm. Examples include floods and heatwaves

q: Exposure is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Exposure: Presence of people, ecosystems or assets in places that could be affected. A component of climate risk

q: Ozone layer is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Ozone layer: Stratospheric region with elevated ozone concentration. Absorbs much harmful ultraviolet radiation

q: Ozone depletion is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Ozone depletion: Reduction in stratospheric ozone. Strongly linked to chlorofluorocarbons

q: Montreal Protocol is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Montreal Protocol: Treaty controlling ozone-depleting substances. Adopted in 1987

q: Paris Agreement is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Paris Agreement: Climate treaty aiming to strengthen global response to climate change. Adopted in 2015

q: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change: Framework treaty for international climate cooperation. Opened for signature in 1992

q: Kyoto Protocol is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Kyoto Protocol: Treaty setting emission targets for many developed countries. Adopted in 1997

q: Convention on Biological Diversity is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Convention on Biological Diversity: Treaty on conservation, sustainable use and benefit-sharing. Opened for signature in 1992

q: CITES is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: CITES: Convention regulating international trade in endangered species. Uses appendices with different protection levels

q: Ramsar Convention is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Ramsar Convention: Treaty for conservation and wise use of wetlands. Adopted in 1971

q: Basel Convention is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Basel Convention: Treaty controlling transboundary movements of hazardous wastes. Adopted in 1989

q: Stockholm Convention is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Stockholm Convention: Treaty controlling persistent organic pollutants. Adopted in 2001

q: Minamata Convention is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Minamata Convention: Treaty protecting health and environment from mercury. Adopted in 2013

q: Desertification is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Desertification: Land degradation in drylands. Driven by climatic variation and human activities

q: Deforestation is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Deforestation: Conversion or removal of forest cover. Reduces habitat and carbon storage

q: Afforestation is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Afforestation: Establishment of forest on land not recently forested. Can increase carbon stocks when appropriately planned

q: Reforestation is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Reforestation: Re-establishment of forest on recently forested land. Supports restoration and carbon sequestration

q: Soil erosion is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Soil erosion: Removal of topsoil by water, wind or other agents. Can reduce agricultural productivity

q: Salinization is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Salinization: Accumulation of salts in soil. Often associated with irrigation and poor drainage

q: Wetland is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Wetland: Land saturated or flooded long enough to support adapted ecosystems. Provides flood regulation and habitat

q: Mangrove is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Mangrove: Salt-tolerant coastal forest ecosystem. Protects shorelines and stores carbon

q: Coral reef is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Coral reef: Marine ecosystem built largely by reef-forming corals. Highly diverse and sensitive to warming

q: Coral bleaching is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Coral bleaching: Loss of symbiotic algae or pigments from stressed corals. Often triggered by heat stress

q: Ocean acidification is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Ocean acidification: Decline in ocean pH caused mainly by absorbed carbon dioxide. Reduces carbonate availability

q: Marine protected area is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Marine protected area: Defined marine area managed for conservation. Protection levels vary

q: IUCN Red List is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: IUCN Red List: Global assessment system for species extinction risk. Uses categories from Least Concern to Extinct

q: Extinct is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Extinct: No reasonable doubt that the last individual has died. Highest final loss category

q: Critically Endangered is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Critically Endangered: Extremely high risk of extinction in the wild. Most severe of the three IUCN threatened categories

q: Endangered is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Endangered: Very high risk of extinction in the wild. Threatened category below Critically Endangered and above Vulnerable

q: Vulnerable is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Vulnerable: High risk of extinction in the wild. Least severe of the three IUCN threatened categories

q: Renewable resource is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Renewable resource: Resource replenished naturally on human timescales. Examples include solar and wind energy

q: Sustainable development is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Sustainable development: Development meeting present needs without compromising future generations. Popularized by the Brundtland Commission

q: Circular economy is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Circular economy: System aiming to reduce waste and keep materials in use. Emphasizes reuse, repair and recycling

q: Ecosystem services is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Ecosystem services: Benefits people obtain from ecosystems. Include provisioning, regulating and cultural services

q: Carbon footprint is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Carbon footprint: Total greenhouse-gas emissions associated with an activity or entity. Often expressed as carbon-dioxide equivalent

q: Ecological footprint is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Ecological footprint: Measure of biologically productive area needed to support consumption and absorb wastes. Compared with biocapacity

q: Life-cycle assessment is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Life-cycle assessment: Assessment of environmental impacts across a product's life cycle. Covers raw materials through disposal

q: Environmental impact assessment is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Environmental impact assessment: Process evaluating likely environmental effects before approval. Supports informed decision-making

q: Pollution is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Pollution: Introduction of harmful substances or energy into the environment. Can affect air, water or land

q: Air pollution is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Air pollution: Contamination of the atmosphere by harmful substances. Includes particulate matter and ozone

q: Particulate matter is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Particulate matter: Mixture of airborne solid particles and liquid droplets. PM2.5 penetrates deeply into lungs

q: Acid rain is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Acid rain: Acidic deposition formed mainly from sulfur and nitrogen oxides. Can acidify soils and waters

q: Smog is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Smog: Air pollution mixture reducing visibility and harming health. Photochemical smog involves ground-level ozone

q: Water pollution is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Water pollution: Contamination degrading water quality. Sources include sewage, industry and agriculture

q: Thermal pollution is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Thermal pollution: Harmful change in water temperature from human activity. Can lower dissolved oxygen

q: Noise pollution is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Noise pollution: Harmful or excessive environmental sound. Can affect health and wildlife

q: Solid waste is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Solid waste: Discarded solid materials from households, industry and other sources. Managed through prevention, reuse, recycling and disposal

q: Hazardous waste is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Hazardous waste: Waste posing substantial risk because of toxic, reactive or other properties. Requires special handling

q: Biodegradable waste is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Biodegradable waste: Waste decomposable by microorganisms. Includes many food and garden wastes

q: Recycling is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Recycling: Processing waste into materials or products. Reduces demand for virgin resources

q: Composting is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Composting: Controlled biological decomposition of organic waste. Produces a soil amendment

q: Landfill is primarily classified under which environmental topic?
e: Landfill: Engineered site for disposal of solid waste. Modern sites use liners and leachate controls
